Give userspace full control of the read-only bits in MISC_ENABLES
do not modify bits on PMU refresh and do not preserve existing bits when
userspace writes MISC_ENABLES.  With a few exceptions where KVM doesn't
expose the necessary controls to userspace _and_ there is a clear cut
association with CPUID
column3: KVM does not own the vCPU

column1: and should not manipulate the vCPU model on behalf of ""dummy user space"".
The argument that KVM is doing userspace a favor because ""the order of
setting vPMU capabilities and MSR_IA32_MISC_ENABLE is not strictly
guaranteed"" is specious
column2: as attempting to configure MSRs on behalf of

column1: userspace inevitably leads to edge cases precisely because KVM does not
prescribe a specific order of initialization.
Example #1: intel_pmu_refresh() consumes and modifies the vCPU's
MSR_IA32_PERF_CAPABILITIES
column2: and so assumes userspace initializes config

column1: MSRs before setting the guest CPUID model.  If userspace sets CPUID
first
column2: then KVM will mark PEBS as available when arch.perf_capabilities

column1: is initialized with a non-zero PEBS format
model if userspace later disables PEBS by writing PERF_CAPABILITIES.
Example #2: intel_pmu_refresh() does not clear PERF_CAP_PEBS_MASK in
MSR_IA32_PERF_CAPABILITIES if there is no vPMU
in its desire to be consistent.
Example #3: intel_pmu_refresh() does not clear MSR_IA32_MISC_ENABLE_EMON
if KVM_SET_CPUID2 is called multiple times
without a vPMU.  While slightly contrived
reflect KVM's default vCPU and then operate on KVM's copy of CPUID to
later clear the vPMU settings
Example #4: Enumerating an Intel vCPU on an AMD host will not call into
intel_pmu_refresh() at any point
column2: and so the BTS and PEBS ""unavailable""

column1: bits will be left clear
column2: without any way for userspace to set them.

column1: Keep the ""R"" behavior of the bit 7
Unlike the BTS and PEBS bits
written with a different value
column2: but that new value is ignored.
